relevance_note: Table 2 lists 50 individual AxD patients with their GFAP mutation, sex and ages: "Information for each patient regarding gender, specific mutation, age of first symptom, age at collection of samples, and age at death (if relevant) is provided in Table 2."
method_note: Cohort biomarker study; all 50 patients in Tables 2-4 (numbered 1-50 under 'Patient no.') are AxD patients with GFAP mutations and are in scope; labels follow rule 1 as 'Patient N' because the text refers to them as 'patient 36', 'Patient 25', 'patients 35 and 50'. Controls (24 CSF, 111 blood) are out of scope and get no rows. A Python script in my scratch directory built rows from my own reading of Tables 2 and 4; spans are exact row prefixes (label through the cited cell), checked verbatim. Table 2: sex, onset, sample ages, age at death and the per-patient Reference column (copied to source_reference_in_review). age_at_last_evaluation is the later of the two sample-collection ages (CSF or blood); this is my interpretation. Table 4 columns: Onset, First symptom, Highest cognitive, Highest motor, Main deterioration, Age at loss of unassisted walking. First-symptom features take the Onset cell as onset. Highest cognitive 'Normal' recorded as intellectual disability excluded (D-27); 'Low normal' (patients 46, 48) not recorded. Highest motor 'Walks without support', 'Normal' and 'Normal gait' not recorded. Main deterioration 'None'/'No' recorded as major deterioration excluded; age at loss of walking 'No' recorded as loss of unassisted walking excluded. ND, N/A, na treated as not reported. Plasma GFAP above the control 95% CI: observed for patient 36 and excluded for the other named patients of the explicitly listed group (1, 8, 13, 22, 29, 31, 35, 38, 40, 49, 50). Unnamed counts (9 of 10 CSF samples elevated; 1 of 5 patients with hydrocephalus; 1 of patients 9, 23, 30, 31) used for no one. Individual CSF/blood GFAP values not recorded as features. Parent-child duos 19-20, 24-25 and 44-45 share the same mutation, but the paper does not say which member is the parent, so inheritance and parental testing are not reported. Patient 45 carries M415I and D157N; the footnote calls D157N 'considered a benign variant' with unknown impact 'in a compound heterozygote'; both rows kept, zygosity not reported. Variants are protein-level only (e.g. R79C), recorded in variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated; no cDNA or transcript printed. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated left null: the authors state 12 CSF and 48 blood patients with 10 overlapping but never a total (Table 2 has 50 rows). Contradictions/inconsistencies: Table 2 vs Table 3 onset for patient 7 ('4*' vs '3.9*'), 36 ('<0.25' vs '0.25*'), 39 ('<1' vs '0.9*'); Table 2 used. Patient 25 onset 'NA' (asymptomatic, familial history). Figure 3 legend refers to ages in 'Table 1' (apparently Table 2). Generic 'weakness' (patients 23, 49) not mapped to limb weakness; 'Vomiting'/'emesis' mapped to recurrent vomiting only where 'frequent' is stated (41). Patient 25 'asymptomatic' not extended to individual checklist items. Pathogenicity footnotes: R105W uncertain (patient 21).
